title: Silent Failure Case
description: One reproducible case where an unattended system reports success while it did not actually verify anything. The case is defined by the gap between reported_verdict and expected_verdict.

id.description: Stable slug. Must equal the filename stem.

title.description: One line, in the contributor's language. No trailing period.

falsifies.description: The existing acceptance criterion this case overturns. Write it as the criterion, not as the bug. Example: 'empty result => nothing to report'.

trigger.description: Preconditions that make the failure reachable. State the system state, not the fix.

observable.description: What an operator actually sees. Include why it fails to raise suspicion.

falsifier.description: A check that would turn green into red. Must be executable or at least decidable, and must state what result falsifies the criterion.

reported_verdict.description: What the system reports today. Free text because implementations differ: 'pass', 'exit 0', 'all green', 'no changes'.

expected_verdict.description: What it should have reported. 'unknown' = evidence missing; 'degraded' = partial but usable; 'blocked' = never finished.

reachability.description: Can a real production path hit this? 'theoretical' cases are still welcome but must be labelled, so hit rates are never aggregated across reachability classes.

domain.description: Short kebab-case tag. Suggested: unattended-loop, filesystem-write, ci-pipeline, document-pipeline, packaging, network-retry, state-machine, encoding.

contributed_by.description: Contributor handle. Use 'anonymous' if you prefer not to be credited.

first_observed.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Date the failure was first seen, not the date of submission.

reference_anchor.description: What the verdict is judged against: a manifest id, a source digest, a sentinel line, a golden file.

normalization_version.description: How inputs and outputs are normalized before comparison. Pin it; otherwise digests are not comparable across batches.

repro.description: Minimal steps or a short code sketch. No credentials, no private paths, no internal URLs.

environment.description: OS / runtime / version, only if the failure depends on it.

notes.description: Boundaries and known limits. Say what this case does NOT prove.

status.description: draft = submitted, format-checked only. reviewed = reproduced by someone other than the contributor. disputed = a counterexample to the falsifier has been reported.
